extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands, comprising 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which uses LLMs to generate data from manual seeds.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The SemanticConflict task involves external data from the ImageNet dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark currently only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control for conflict degree, and does not study attention mechanisms.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to recognize conflicting commands.

name.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands.

description.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: It is constructed by a novel automatic dataset creation framework, which expedites the process and enables us to encompass a wide range of instruction forms.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Within 8 types of conflicts, only SemanticConflict involves extemal data, ImageNet.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs).

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Our work on the SCIbenchmark, along with the AutoCreate framework and CaPapproach, has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs’ ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: To begin with, we only include language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in our SCIbenchmark based on our automatic framework, AutoCreate . Besides, no fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree.
